A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GFlowNet loss-design work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including the new Appendix F in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original hyper-grid, bit-sequence generation, and molecule-generation experiments, with numerical results and learning curves.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds 5D hyper-grid results and experiments with additional loss functions in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Appendix F substantially expands the proposed objective repertoire with five implemented and evaluated losses: forward chi-square, reverse chi-square, total variation, symmetric KL, and Jensen-Shannon. These change the regression objective within the retained framework; the original three proposed losses and model architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section 5.1 adds a 5D hyper-grid alongside the original 4D environment, increasing the state space, available coordinate actions, and reward modes. Bit-sequence and molecule-generation coverage is unchanged; Appendix F reuses the existing bit-sequence task.

E2.justification: Tables 7–8 substantially broaden the bit-sequence comparison with five additional divergence-based loss alternatives under TB, DB, and STB. Reverse KL, forward KL, and Hellinger retain the original Quadratic, Linex(1), and Linex(1/2) comparators under different names.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same metrics, sampling procedures, architectures, and training budgets. Appendix E is unchanged, and Appendix F refers back to the existing bit-sequence evaluation procedure. The additional grid dimension changes environment coverage rather than the retained evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The new 5D experiment tests robustness to a harder exploration environment. Appendix F also extends the loss analysis beyond one representative per zero-forcing/zero-avoiding category, testing whether the observed behaviors persist across additional objectives with matching properties.

E5.justification: Appendix E retains three random-seed runs for hyper-grid, five for bit sequences, and four for molecules. The added tables follow the existing success-count and plus/minus reporting practices, including exclusion of collapsed runs from correlation reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds 5D results showing failure of the quadratic baseline across the displayed algorithms. Tables 7–8 add substantial results for five losses: forward chi-square finds all modes in 5/5 runs for each algorithm, with median steps of 80.3k, 8.1k, and 10.2k for TB, DB, and STB; reverse chi-square achieves 0/5 for each. Original results in Tables 3–4 and Figures 4–5 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Remark 4.2 adds the requirement that the convex regression loss be minimized at zero. Appendix F supplies additional divergence-to-loss correspondences and their zero-forcing/zero-avoiding properties through applications of the existing framework. The central theorems and proofs in Appendices B–D remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a unified training framework, a correspondence with divergence measures, three highlighted losses, and improved behavior across three benchmark families. The additional experiments and loss examples support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly interprets losses sharing zero-forcing or zero-avoiding properties as producing similar behaviors. Section 4.3 also explicitly discusses loss validity across choices of other training components. The existing exploration–exploitation interpretation and main limitations discussion otherwise remain.

D1.justification: Appendix E preserves the implementation sources, architectures, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, training durations, and estimation details. There is no new code or data access information or additional hardware disclosure.

R1.justification: Related Work adds discussion of Silva et al.'s divergence-based GFlowNet research and more explicitly explains the extension of Malkin et al. New citations also include Zimmermann, Hellinger, and Genetic-GFN. Numerous other reference changes are publication-metadata updates to already cited works.

P1.justification: Related Work is locally reorganized and rewritten, explanatory passages are added around loss validity, and Appendix F extends the document structure. Most main-text prose and the existing appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains a second row of 5D panels, and Tables 6–8 are added. Existing figures are relocated or resized, and Table 4 changes row order while retaining its values. The overall visual format remains consistent.

improvement.justification: The harder-grid test and additional loss comparisons provide useful evidence about the framework's breadth and robustness. The corrected condition in Remark 4.2 and clearer positioning against related work also improve precision. These gains are incremental because the central theoretical argument, original experiments, and reproducibility information are largely retained.
